faq.v: Can I hire a bike or e-bike from you?
faq.a: Yes. At reception you can hire a regular bike or an e-bike. Let us know when you book or when you arrive, and we will have it ready for you.

faq.v: Where can I leave my own bike?
faq.a: In our locked, covered bike storage next to the hotel. If you had a flat tyre on the way, we will lend you a pump and a repair kit.

faq.v: Can I charge my e-bike at the hotel?
faq.a: Yes. You can charge your battery with us, so you set off fully charged again the next morning. Reception will show you where.

faq.v: How do I take the routes with me?
faq.a: Each route opens with the button next to it on Fietsknoop or routiq, on your phone too. Free cycling and walking routes on paper are available at reception.

faq.v: Which route is best to start with?
faq.a: The Venray loop: 24.5 kilometres on the junction network right by the hotel, past the Annapark and over the Weverslose Berg, the highest point in North Limburg.

rondje-venray.alt: Terraces on the Grote Markt in Venray with the Sint-Petrus' Bandenkerk
rondje-venray.tekst: A loop around Venray that starts on the junction network next to the hotel. You cycle past the Annapark, the listed park of the former Sint Anna, and through the hamlet of Weverslo to the Weverslose Berg: at 38.6 metres the highest point in North Limburg, with a viewpoint at the top. At junction 23 you can cut straight through to the town centre.

rondje-over-het-pontje.alt: A cyclist pointing out a route on the junction network sign
rondje-over-het-pontje.tekst: A short ride with the Maas at its heart. In Maashees you sit by the water at De Watervogel, then cycle to the Reindersmeer in De Maasduinen National Park and look across the gardens at the moated castle Kasteel Well. The little ferry takes you across the Maas and you ride back via Geijsteren; check beforehand whether the ferry is running.

alts.fotos/l26-omg-maasduinen-2.webp: Water and woodland in De Maasduinen National Park

langs-de-maas.alt: A couple cycling along a forest path near Venray
langs-de-maas.tekst: Via Oostrum and Parc de Witte Vennen you cycle to Meerlo, with the Sint-Goarkapel from 1662 and Slothoeve 't Kasteelke. At Tante Jet aan de Maas, one of the oldest cafés on the river, the foot and bike ferry docks; it runs from 1 April to 14 October inclusive. You return through Geijsteren.

van-venray-naar-de-peel.alt: A couple pointing at something between the trees
van-venray-naar-de-peel.tekst: From Venray into the Peel, past the Weverslose Berg and the Rouwvennen nature area. At junction 25 lies the German war cemetery at Ysselsteyn, with a visitor centre. You then cycle along the Heere Peel and through the Schadijkse bossen to the centre of Venray, 3 kilometres from the hotel.

rondje-horst-aan-de-maas.alt: Two cyclists on the drive of Hotel Asteria
rondje-horst-aan-de-maas.tekst: A loop through Horst aan de Maas with a stop in Tienray, also known as Little Lourdes: church, small chapels and the Clevers ice cream parlour. The route then winds through the Schuitwater nature area with woods, heath and water, and along the Kasteelse Bossen. You finish among the terraces in the centre of Venray.

maasduinen-en-arcen.tekst: A day trip to Arcen. Via Geijsteren you cycle to the Maas and through De Maasduinen National Park, past the lookout tower at Wellerlooi. In Arcen the Kasteeltuinen, the old fortified town and the Hertog Jan Brouwerij with its tasting room await. The bike ferry along the way runs from 10 April to 14 October inclusive.

ballonzuilbossen-en-overloon.alt: The Ballonzuil monument in the Ballonzuilbossen near Merselo
ballonzuilbossen-en-overloon.tekst: A long loop that starts at the Grote Kerk in Venray, 3 kilometres from the hotel. Past the Annapark you cycle to Smakt with the Sint-Jozefkapel from 1699, and along the Overloonse Duinen to Overloon with the British war cemetery, the Liberty Park and ZooParc. The way back takes you through the Ballonzuilbossen.

rondje-venray-via-vierlingsbeek.alt: A chapel among the pines on a forest path
rondje-venray-via-vierlingsbeek.tekst: This route starts in Overloon, home of the Liberty Park. You cycle through the Overloonse Duinen to Maashees on the Maas, past tree nurseries and the Willibrorduskapel in the woods of Landgoed Geijsteren. Through the centre of Venray and the Peel village of Merselo you return to Overloon.

meterik-venray-horst.alt: An oak beside a narrow road through the meadows in the morning mist
meterik-venray-horst.tekst: A long ride through the woods and floodplains of the Maas between Meterik, Venray and Horst. On the way you cycle across Landgoed Geijsteren, owned by the same family for more than two centuries, where the Oostrumse Beek winds through the pine forests.

door-de-peel-bij-horst.alt: A drawbridge over a canal in the Peel
door-de-peel-bij-horst.tekst: Along quiet roads through Castenray and Veulen into the Peel. At De Paardekop lies the German military cemetery, and in the Toon Kortoomspark you can read about the writer. Via Griendtsveen and Helenaveen, the two old peat colonies of the southern Netherlands, you ride past the raised bog of the Deurnsche Peel and the Mariapeel.
